thread:
deploybot: Releasecheck: holding release/2026.04.02 - env-overlay parity failure detected :rotating_light: S3_BUCKET_SUFFIX and KMS_ALIAS differ between staging and prod overlays. Risk: canary writes may target wrong bucket or fail KMS decrypts.

maria: @deploybot can you paste the exact diff?

deploybot: Overlay diff:
```yaml
staging.values.yaml:
  S3_BUCKET_SUFFIX: "us-west-logs-2026"
  KMS_ALIAS: "alias/redwood-staging"
prod.values.yaml:
  S3_BUCKET_SUFFIX: "us-prod-logs"
  KMS_ALIAS: "alias/redwood-prod"
```

josh: Oof. If the running canary is wired to prod KMS but points at a staging bucket (or vice-versa) we get upload fails or unreadable objects. Who made the overlay change?

priya: That was me. I updated the chart to split ingestion per-region; I only promoted the staging overlay to validate a pipeline change and missed syncing prod. I thought the release bundling would pick it up. My bad.

opsbot: Canary at 1% (eu-central) - recent logs show KMS errors and 400s.
```
[2026-04-02T09:12:10Z] uploader-2 ERROR upload failed: 403 KMS AccessDenied for key alias/redwood-prod
[2026-04-02T09:12:12Z] uploader-2 WARN fallback-upload failed: 400 BadRequest bucket name mismatch: expected us-prod-logs got us-west-logs-2026
```

maria: Change window closes in 75m. Options: 1) rollback image -> stops canary progress but safe, 2) patch overlay to match prod values (quick hotpatch) -> risks touching prod KMS, 3) flip FF to disable log-sink writes for canary -> lowest risk, but we lose logs for canary.

priya: I can open a revert PR to restore the previous consistent overlay (should be ~15m). Also can add a short-lived FF `log-sink.canary.off=true` now.

josh: Revert PR + FF toggle sounds best. Avoid hotpatching KMS alias in prod overlays during the window.

deploybot: Action: Rollout paused by @maria at ts=2769130200. release/2026.04.02 state=PAUSED. Canary traffic for new image scaled to 0%.

priya: Opening PR now: "revert: restore s3/kms overlay parity for release/2026.04.02" - tagging ops and maria. ETA ~20m. Also creating FF and toggling for canary.

maria: Please also add a post-check in the release pipeline to detect mismatched critical keys: S3_BUCKET_SUFFIX, KMS_ALIAS, S3_REGION. This would have been caught by a simple parity lint.

opsbot: Created ticket INT-4999: "release-check: overlay key parity lint for S3/KMS values". Assigned to @josh.

josh: I'll scope a small release-check rule and a warning in the short-term. If we can't ship the lint before next deploy, add the check to the release notes and run a manual parity check.

priya: PR up: https://github.com/redwood/release-charts/pull/432 (revert overlay). I also pushed FF toggle `log-sink.canary.off=true` and verified it via dev-console.

maria: Thanks. Once chart revert merges and passes CI, we can resume canary at low percent and re-run smoke tests. Ops: notify CS about potential missing logs for affected canaries.

opsbot: Notified #customer-impact: "Canaries for release/2026.04.02 had log ingestion disabled briefly due to env-overlay mismatch. No user traffic impacted. Follow-up: INT-4999 created." :white_check_mark:

maria: Postmortem/Triage: schedule a 30m follow-up tomorrow to review release workflow and gating. Add retro item: require explicit overlay promotion step.

priya: Sorry team. Will add a checklist item to the release playbook and update the PR template to call out overlay parity.

josh: Good catch by releasecheck. Closing loop: we should also add `critical-overlay-keys` to service metadata so release-check can iterate them per-service.

maria: Closing thread for now. Resume candidate once revert passes. :thumbsup:
